tasks.title: Liked Songs uses Spotify's /me/library endpoints with track URIs, a refusal recovers, and the Premium copy stops blaming the listener
tasks.why: Since 2026-03-09 Spotify serves PUT/DELETE /me/library and GET /me/library/contains (uris=, max 40, comma-separated) in place of /me/tracks and /me/tracks/contains for Development Mode apps (migration guide and the three reference pages, read 2026-10-11). The heart therefore never works for anyone on the built-in client. Separately, refuse() latches apiBlocked for the life of the process: disconnect() and a new grant never clear it, the heart's .task is the only caller of refreshSavedState and is not drawn while blocked, so a fixed account never recovers. Both defects live in the same functions (refreshSavedState, toggleSaved, refuse, Refusal, disconnect), so this is one task.
tasks.failing_test_first: In SpotifyAccountTests (stubbed URLSession, throwaway CredentialStore): (1) testSavedStateAsksTheLibraryWithATrackURI: the stub answers 200 "[true]" only for GET /v1/me/library/contains whose uris query is spotify:track:<id>, and 404 for anything else; after refreshSavedState, saved[id] == true. It fails today twice over: the old path, and refreshSavedState uses URLSession.shared so the stub is never reached. (2) testToggleSavedPutsThenDeletesTheTrackURI: records method and path; PUT then DELETE /v1/me/library?uris=spotify:track:<id>; saved flips and stays. (3) testARefusedAccountRecoversAfterTheCooldown: 403 then 200, injected clock advanced 601 s, a second refreshSavedState clears apiBlocked and refusal and fills saved. (4) testNothingIsAskedInsideTheCooldown: request count stays 1 at +599 s. (5) testDisconnectClearsTheRefusal: after a 403, disconnect() leaves apiBlocked false, refusal nil, tokenUnavailable false. (6) testANewGrantClearsTheRefusal: drive beginAuthorization through an injected openURL seam that captures the URL, then handleCallback with its state and a stubbed 200 token exchange. In FindabilityTests: testAPremiumRefusalDoesNotAddressTheListener asserts the .premiumRequired explanation is the new key.
tasks.approach: 1. Inject the existing `session` into refreshSavedState and toggleSaved (both use URLSession.shared today). This is the test seam, and it is also where G-016's ephemeral-session fix will land. 2. Build URLs with URLComponents: GET https://api.spotify.com/v1/me/library/contains?uris=spotify:track:<id>, and PUT or DELETE https://api.spotify.com/v1/me/library?uris=spotify:track:<id>. Validate the id as 22 base62 characters before building, because it comes from AppleScript. The response stays a [Bool]. Keep GET /v1/tracks/{id} for trackMetadata, which the guide keeps. 3. Latch: add `blockedUntil: Date?` and an injected `now: () -> Date` (default Date.init). refuse() sets blockedUntil = now + 600 s. A private mayAsk(now) is true when not blocked or when the cooldown has passed. refreshSavedState and trackMetadata guard on mayAsk instead of !apiBlocked. A success clears apiBlocked and blockedUntil, as today. disconnect() and a completed exchange (a new grant, not a token refresh) reset apiBlocked, blockedUntil and tokenUnavailable; apiBlocked's didSet already clears refusal. Fix the doc comment at :34-36. 4. LockScreenCard: move `.task(id:)` from the heart Button to the header HStack, so refreshSavedState still runs (and probes after the cooldown) while the heart is hidden. The heart's drawing condition does not change. 5. Copy: keep the case name .premiumRequired and rewrite its explanation so the Premium is placed on Isla's registration, not on the listener's plan. 6. Add an openURL seam (default NSWorkspace.shared.open) to beginAuthorization so the grant path is testable; KX-02 reuses it. 7. Checklist: date-stamp the Spotify capability bullet (endpoints moved to /me/library) and add an S10 step to the live script: the heart's status codes for contains, PUT and DELETE with the built-in client and a listed account. Amend the design doc's 2026-09-23 refusal sentence in place, dated. Rejected: keeping /me/tracks until a live call proves it fails, because Spotify's guide states the replacement and the date. Clearing the latch on every token refresh, because a refresh is not a new grant and would re-enable the API about once an hour. Drawing a dimmed heart while blocked so its own .task probes, because it flickers and shows a control that cannot act. Adding user-follow-read, playlist-read-private and the other listed scopes, because the guide says scopes depend on the entity saved and new scopes would force every connected user to consent again; this is checked live instead.
tasks.acceptance: `swift test --filter SpotifyAccountTests` and `--filter FindabilityTests` pass, including the six new cases. No Sources file mentions /me/tracks. ./scripts/check passes (the localization gate shows the old Premium key removed and the new key in en and ru). On the owner's live run (S10) with a listed account, the lock-card heart fills for a liked song and a tap round-trips. After a forced 403 and Disconnect, then Connect, the Settings note is gone.
tasks.risks: G-010 (silent sign-in failures, revoked grant) and G-032 (writes race, disconnect does not stop an in-flight lookup) edit the same SpotifyAccount functions; schedule this first in that lane or rebase on them. G-016 swaps the session type; this task only routes the two calls through the injected session, so the conflict is trivial. Whether /me/library/contains accepts the current two scopes for track URIs, and what text the Development Mode 403 carries, are live-only. If Spotify now demands extra scopes, that is an account-scope change, which belongs in checklist.md and with the owner (see deferred).
tasks.strings_and_tokens: Remove key "Spotify refused this account. Liked Songs needs Spotify Premium." (en and ru). Add en: "Spotify refused Liked Songs and named Premium. Spotify asks this of Isla's own registration, so your plan may not be the cause." ru: "Spotify отказал в «Любимых треках» и сослался на Premium. Spotify требует его от регистрации самой Isla, так что дело может быть не в вашей подписке." Shown through localized() in Refusal.explanation. No style tokens change.

tasks.title: Spotify sign-in survives a second Connect, always offers a choice of account, and says when it could not open the browser, import or save
tasks.why: beginAuthorization overwrites the verifier and state on every press, so approving the first browser tab fails the state check and returns silently. Without show_dialog, a reconnect after Disconnect silently reuses the browser's signed-in account. NSWorkspace.open's result is ignored. importLegacy reports success if any one of three items moved, after which the Import row is hidden. TokenStore.write failures are dropped, and store() still claims to be connected.
tasks.failing_test_first: In SpotifyAccountTests, using the openURL seam from KX-01 to capture URLs, a stub token endpoint and a throwaway store: (1) testASecondConnectKeepsTheFirstTabValid: call beginAuthorization twice; both captured URLs carry the same state; handleCallback with the first URL's state and a code, with token 200, gives isConnected true. Today the second press rotates the state and the callback is dropped. (2) testTheConsentPageAlwaysOffersAnotherAccount: the captured URL has show_dialog=true. (3) testABrowserThatDoesNotOpenIsSaid: openURL returns false, so signInProblem == .browserDidNotOpen. (4) testAPartialImportIsNotASuccess: pure `CredentialStore.importSucceeded(moved:)` is false for ["accessToken","expiresAt"] and true only when "refreshToken" moved. (5) testUnsavedTokensDoNotClaimAConnection: pure `SpotifyAccount.connectedAfterStore(refreshBacking:)` is false for .unavailable.
tasks.approach: 1. Pending flow: beginAuthorization reuses the existing verifier and state while they are younger than 10 minutes (store a createdAt), and makes a new pair only after expiry or after a completed callback. Both tabs then carry one valid state; the first approval consumes it, and the later tab's callback is ignored, which is correct. 2. Always add show_dialog=true to the authorize URL. Connect is offered only while disconnected, so the cost is one extra approval click on a reconnect, and in exchange Spotify shows its 'Not you?' switch. 3. Add `@Published private(set) var signInProblem: SignInProblem?` with .browserDidNotOpen, .importIncomplete and .tokensNotSaved. It is set from openURL's Bool, from importLegacy's verdict (the row stays offered on failure), and from storeTokens, which now returns the refresh write's TokenStore.Backing (write already returns it). It is cleared on the next Connect press or on success. 4. SettingsPane shows signInProblem as one noteRow in the Spotify section. A section-level failure is an inline note, per the one-failure-surface rule, with no toast. Rejected: keeping several pending verifiers keyed by state, which is more state and more attack surface for the same outcome. Passing show_dialog only after a disconnect, which needs a persisted flag and still misses a keychain-lost reconnect. A toast for these failures, because the Settings row is where the user acted.
tasks.acceptance: The five tests pass, and `swift test --filter SpotifyAccountTests` stays green. ./scripts/check passes, including the localization gate with three new keys in en and ru. Live (S2 or S10 in the owner script): press Connect twice, approve the first tab, and the account connects; Disconnect then Connect shows Spotify's consent page with a way to switch account.
tasks.risks: G-010 also adds a sign-in failure surface (access_denied, tokenUnavailable text) on the same Spotify row. Whichever lands second must fold into one SignInProblem enum, never two notes for one event. show_dialog=true is documented Spotify behaviour; confirm on the consent page live.
tasks.strings_and_tokens: en "Isla could not open your browser for Spotify sign-in." / ru "Isla не смогла открыть браузер для входа в Spotify."; en "The account was not imported. Try again, or connect it anew." / ru "Учётная запись не перенесена. Повторите попытку или подключите её заново."; en "Spotify signed you in, but Isla could not save the account on this Mac." / ru "Вход в Spotify выполнен, но Isla не смогла сохранить учётную запись на этом Mac." All through localized(). The noteRow is the existing primitive.

tasks.title: Peeks and charger and headphone moments stay quiet while an app is full screen, a presentation hides the menu bar, or the display is mirrored
tasks.why: sneakPeek and ambientAllowed have no input for full screen, presentation or mirroring. The panel is .canJoinAllSpaces with .fullScreenAuxiliary at statusWindow+1, and sharingType = .none does not hide it from a hardware mirror. A song title or battery level therefore lands on a projector or over a film. activeSpaceChanged folds an open panel but leaves a peek or moment that is already running. The island's own presence on every Space (S9-b) is the tested contract and is not touched.
tasks.failing_test_first: New QuietMomentsTests for the pure `QuietMoments.isQuiet(switchOn:presentation:mirrored:focusQuiet:)`: testAFullScreenAppIsQuiet (.fullScreen), testAHiddenMenuBarIsQuiet (.hideMenuBar, as a slideshow sets it), testAMirroredDisplayIsQuiet, testAnAutoHiddenMenuBarAloneIsNotQuiet (.autoHideMenuBar only), testTheSwitchOffLetsMomentsThrough, testFocusQuietHoldsEvenWithTheSwitchOff, and testTheSwitchDefaultsOn (key absent, so true). In AmbientMomentTests, extend testTheMomentKeepsTheTrackPeeksRestraint with `quiet: true`, which must be refused; it fails to compile until the parameter exists. Add testTheTrackPeekKeepsTheSameRestraint against a new pure `NotchController.peekAllowed(enabled:isOpen:isDropTargeted:ambientShowing:isLocked:pointerInside:pillVisible:quiet:)`, one assertion per refusal.
tasks.approach: 1. QuietMoments (an enum with static functions, nonisolated where pure). `isQuiet` returns focusQuiet, or else switchOn and (presentation contains .fullScreen or .hideMenuBar, or mirrored). `current(screen:)` reads NSApp.currentSystemPresentationOptions, which Apple documents as the options the active app has in effect system-wide, and CGDisplayIsInMirrorSet for the island's display (geometry.screen's NSScreenNumber). It reads them by pull, at gate time, with no observers or polling. focusQuiet is read from a defaults key that KX-04 writes and that is false until then. 2. NotchViewModel gains quietInFullScreenKey ("island.quietInFullScreen") and quietInFullScreenEnabled, defaulting to true, on the showChargingEnabled pattern. 3. sneakPeek: replace the guard chain with peekAllowed(...) plus `quiet: QuietMoments.current(...)`. presentAmbient: pass quiet into ambientAllowed. 4. activeSpaceChanged: after the existing repair, cut any running peek or moment (cancel peekWork and set isPeeking false; call clearAmbient()). Entering a full-screen Space is a Space change, so a peek already running does not follow the user into a film. 5. Settings: one toggleRow, 'Quiet in Full Screen', in General below 'Show Headphones Connecting', with SettingsIcon.quietInFullScreen = "arrow.up.left.and.arrow.down.right". 6. Add a dated design-doc amendment after 'the island without music' (2026-09-23), a checklist.md entry (default on, nothing leaves the Mac, no system setting changed) and a live-script S12 step: Keynote play mirrored, a full-screen film, and a game, each with a track change and a charger plug. Rejected: hiding the resting pill in full screen, which contradicts S9-b. CGWindowList scans for a screen-sized window, which run per gate and judge by geometry. CGDisplayIsCaptured, which is deprecated and which modern full-screen games do not trigger (they set .fullScreen). KVO on presentation options, which adds a live observer for a decision that is only needed at two moments. Per-display full-screen detection, because the presentation options are system-wide and the gap (a full-screen app on the other display) only makes the island quieter, never louder.
tasks.acceptance: `swift test --filter QuietMomentsTests` and `--filter AmbientMomentTests` pass. ./scripts/check passes (localization gate: one new key in en and ru; TabContractTests untouched). Live S12: the pill is still present over a full-screen Safari, but a track change shows no peek; Keynote play to a mirrored projector shows no peek or charger moment; with the switch off, peeks return.
tasks.risks: F-033 (moment not cleared on panel open), G-033 (flapping charger) and F-013 (VoiceOver announcements for peeks and moments) edit sneakPeek, presentAmbient and clearAmbient. Schedule this in the a11y-shell lane and land it first or rebase. Whether .hideMenuBar is what Keynote and PowerPoint set while playing, and whether the panel sits above their play windows, is live-only (round-3 'what remains'). The memory note on xctest's defaults leak means the default-on test must set aside and restore the key.
tasks.strings_and_tokens: en "Quiet in Full Screen" / ru "Тишина в полноэкранном режиме" through localized(). Icon through SettingsIcon. The row is the shared toggleRow primitive. No new colours or radii.

tasks.title: A Focus can quiet Isla's peeks and moments through a Focus filter beside the App Intents
tasks.why: K-003's last part: a user in a Sleep or Work Focus still gets every moment. SetFocusFilterIntent (macOS 13+) is the documented route. The system calls perform() with the configured values when the Focus turns on and with the defaults when it turns off. No permission and no network.
tasks.failing_test_first: (1) QuietMomentsTests.testAFocusFilterTurnsQuietOnAndItsEndTurnsItOff: `QuietMoments.setFocusQuiet(true, defaults: suite)` makes `focusQuiet(defaults: suite)` true, false after setFocusQuiet(false), and a fresh suite reads false. Use a throwaway UserDefaults suite. (2) Scripts/test-package.sh: add IslaFocusFilter to the `for INTENT in ...` grep list, which fails until the intent is declared and bundle.sh's metadata pass extracts it.
tasks.approach: Declare `struct IslaFocusFilter: SetFocusFilterIntent` in IslaIntents.swift: static title "Quiet Isla", description, `@Parameter(title: "Hide Peeks and Moments", default: false) var hidesMoments: Bool`, and a displayRepresentation whose title depends on the value. perform() calls QuietMoments.setFocusQuiet(hidesMoments) (UserDefaults key "focus.quietMoments"), which KX-03's gate already reads. The default is false because the system calls perform() with default values when the Focus ends. It stays inside IslaIntents.swift so the localization gate's intent scrape (title:, LocalizedStringResource, IntentDescription) sees every string. Record it in checklist.md (reads Focus state the user configured; default off, because nothing happens until the user adds the filter in System Settings › Focus), add a dated design amendment and a live-script step. Rejected: reading Focus through INFocusStatusCenter, which needs a permission prompt and only gives on or off with no per-Focus choice. Making the filter also hide the resting island, which is not asked for and touches S9-b.
tasks.acceptance: The new unit test passes. ./scripts/check passes: test-package.sh finds IslaFocusFilter in Metadata.appintents and the localization gate covers the four new keys in en and ru. Live: System Settings › Focus › Sleep › Focus Filters lists Isla. With 'Hide Peeks and Moments' on and Sleep on, a track change shows no peek; with Sleep off, peeks return.
tasks.risks: Focus filters on macOS may only list apps whose metadata the system has indexed from /Applications. Install through Scripts/install.sh before the live check. perform() can launch the accessory app if it is not running, which is the same contract the other intents state.
tasks.strings_and_tokens: en "Quiet Isla" / ru "Тихая Isla"; en "Hide Peeks and Moments" / ru "Скрывать показы и моменты"; en "Peeks and moments hidden" / ru "Показы и моменты скрыты"; en "Peeks and moments as usual" / ru "Показы и моменты как обычно"; IntentDescription en "Keeps track peeks and charger and headphone moments off the island during this Focus." / ru "Во время этого режима фокусирования показы треков, зарядки и наушников не появляются на острове."

tasks.title: Translate stops presenting a stale answer or failure as current: Retry reacts at once, Copy copies only the translation of the text on screen, and resolvable obstacles offer Retry
tasks.why: translate() never clears output or failure when it starts, and the pane shows the failure first and the spinner only when both are empty. Retry therefore changes nothing on screen for 320 ms plus the engine's time. copyOutput copies output even when outputSource no longer matches the input. .appleIntelligenceOff, .modelNotReady and .needsDownload offer no Retry after the user fixes the cause elsewhere.
tasks.failing_test_first: In TranslatorTests: (1) testCopyRefusesAnAnswerToOtherText: received("Привет", for: "Hello", by: .system), then input = "Hello there"; answersInput is false and copyOutput() returns false (copyOutput is changed to return Bool, so the test never touches NSPasteboard). (2) testRetryClearsTheFailureAtOnce: a capabilitiesOverride with no engines, await translate(), so failure is non-nil; retry() leaves failure nil, remedies empty and isTranslating true. (3) testResolvableObstaclesOfferRetry: remedies(for: .appleIntelligenceOff) contains .retry, as do .modelNotReady and .needsDownload; .deviceNotEligible does not. (4) testTheWorkingStateBeatsAStaleFailure: pure `Translator.display(failure:output:answersInput:isTranslating:)` returns .working when isTranslating and the failure belongs to an earlier run, and .answer(stale: true) for an output that does not answer the input.
tasks.approach: Translator: add `var answersInput: Bool { !output.isEmpty && outputSource == trimmed }`. copyOutput guards on it and returns Bool. retry() clears failure and remedies and raises isTranslating before bumping attempt; translate()'s generation-stamped defer lowers it, and schedule()'s clear() lowers it if the text empties. translate() clears failure and remedies when a run starts, and keeps a stale output on screen until it is replaced. remedies(for:) appends .retry to the three obstacles the user can fix outside Isla. Add a pure `display(...)` enum (.failure, .answer(stale:), .working, .empty). TranslatePane.outcome switches on it. A stale answer is drawn in Theme.tertiary instead of white, and the Copy button shows only when answersInput. Rejected: blanking the output on every keystroke, which makes the column flash for every letter, and the swap already relies on outputSource. Overlaying a spinner on the old failure, which puts two states in one column. Retry on .deviceNotEligible, which can never succeed.
tasks.acceptance: The four tests pass; `swift test --filter TranslatorTests` stays green. ./scripts/check passes. By hand on a macOS 26 Mac: after 'The translation could not be completed.', Retry shows 'Translating…' at once. Editing a translated sentence dims the old translation and hides Copy until the new one lands.
tasks.risks: F-042 rewrites which failures offer Retry (the engine-loop end and describe), G-026 adds an outputSource check that skips re-translating unchanged text in schedule() and translate(), and H-007 restyles the remedy buttons in remedyButton(). All four edit the same functions, so schedule this right after them in the visual-translate lane. F-002 and F-021 (privacy cover) edit the same outcome view.
tasks.strings_and_tokens: No new strings: Retry and Translating… exist. A stale answer uses the existing Theme.tertiary token. No raw opacity or hex.

tasks.title: On macOS 15 the Translate Online note says that everything goes to MyMemory
tasks.why: Below macOS 26, capabilities() reports nothing on device, so engines() routes every pair online. The note under the switch still says that only languages 'such as Uzbek' leave the Mac. Routing is deliberate and correct; only the note misleads about what leaves the machine.
tasks.failing_test_first: TranslatorTests.testBelowMacOS26TheOnlineNoteSaysEverythingLeaves: pure `Translator.onlineNote(onlineEnabled: true, translatesOnDevice: false)` returns the new key's text; with translatesOnDevice true it returns the existing Uzbek note; with onlineEnabled false it returns 'Translations stay on this Mac.'
tasks.approach: Move the note choice out of SettingsPane into the pure Translator.onlineNote. SettingsPane passes `translatesOnDevice: ProcessInfo.processInfo.isOperatingSystemAtLeast(OperatingSystemVersion(majorVersion: 26, minorVersion: 0, patchVersion: 0))`, which is the same boundary capabilities() uses. Rejected: changing the off-state note too, a wider copy change than the finding. Moving the disclosure onto the switch title, which would differ by OS for one row.
tasks.acceptance: The test passes; ./scripts/check passes with one new key in en and ru. On a macOS 15 VM, Settings › Translate with Translate Online on shows the new sentence.
tasks.risks: Only SettingsPane's Translate section is touched. Other lanes edit other SettingsPane sections, so expect textual merge conflicts only.
tasks.strings_and_tokens: en "Before macOS 26 this Mac cannot translate on its own, so everything you translate is sent to MyMemory over the internet." / ru "До macOS 26 этот Mac не переводит сам, поэтому всё, что вы переводите, отправляется в MyMemory через интернет." Through localized().

tasks.title: Text with ї, є or ґ is detected as Ukrainian
tasks.why: byLetters settles only Kazakh and Uzbek letters. Short Ukrainian text needs recognizer confidence of 0.95 or more, and otherwise falls back to 'Cyrillic is Russian'. ї, є and ґ are written by no other offered Cyrillic language (Russian, Kazakh, Uzbek).
tasks.failing_test_first: LanguageDetectionTests.testUkrainianOnlyLettersSettleUkrainian: LanguageDetection.language(of:) is .ukrainian for "Їжак", "Є", "ґанок" and "Я їм". It stays not Ukrainian for "Сіз қалайсыз?" (Kazakh, settled earlier) and for a string mixing ї with ы. Translator.route(for: "Їжак", source: nil, target: .russian) is uk→ru, not ru→en.
tasks.approach: In byLetters, after the Kazakh and Uzbek rules: if the text contains ї, є or ґ and none of ы, ё, ъ or э, return .ukrainian. Update the doc comment, which today says і alone decides nothing, to name the three letters that do. Rejected: lowering shortTextConfidence for Ukrainian, which is a recognizer guess rather than a rule and would mislabel 'Друг'.
tasks.acceptance: The test passes; `swift test --filter LanguageDetectionTests` and `--filter TranslatorTests` stay green; ./scripts/check passes.
tasks.risks: G-014 (detection decided by one character from another script) edits language(of:) right next to this. The rule here sits in byLetters and should not conflict, but run both lanes' tests together. 'Дякую' has none of the three letters and stays recognizer-dependent (see deferred).

tasks.why: test-localizations.sh scrapes only localized("…"), Button("…"), the welcome Copy block and the intent titles. Text, Label, Toggle, Picker, .help and .accessibility* literals are invisible to it. Equal en and ru values are rejected only for InfoPlist.strings. The locale loops hard-code en and ru while bundle.sh copies every Resources/*.lproj and declares CFBundleLocalizations [en, ru]. Today no bare literal exists and only Spotify and AirDrop are equal in both tables (checked 2026-10-11), so the hole is latent.
files: Scripts/localization_gate.py (new, the Python body moved out of the heredoc)
Scripts/fixtures/localization-gate/ (new: bare-literal, copied-ru, third-lproj fixture roots)

tasks.title: The lock-card volume bar appears only for a device whose volume can be set, and a drag never follows a new default output
tasks.why: SystemVolume.current() decides that the bar exists from AudioObjectHasProperty plus a read and never checks AudioObjectIsPropertySettable. set() checks it, but both callers ignore its false, so on a fixed-volume DAC or HDMI output the bar moves and snaps back, which is the 'slider that moves and changes nothing' the file rules out. set() re-reads the default output on every call, so AirPods arriving mid-drag receive the finger's absolute level.
tasks.failing_test_first: New SystemVolumeTests on a pure `SystemVolume.level(main:left:right:)` taking optional (value, settable) controls: testAReadOnlyMainControlHasNoBar (main read-only and no channels gives nil), testSettableChannelsAverage, and testReadOnlyChannelsAreIgnored. In the card, a pure `LockScreenCard.volumeDragTarget(latched:current:)` returns latched only while it equals current: testADragEndsWhenTheDefaultOutputChanges.
tasks.approach: SystemVolume: read value and settable together for each control. current() returns a level only from settable controls, and the bar's existing 'absent entirely' contract then holds. Add set(_:on:) taking an explicit device; set(_:) keeps its current-device path for the accessibility step. LockScreenCard volumeBar: latch the device from currentOutput on the first onChanged, write through set(_:on:), and end the drag (draggingVolume nil, re-read) when the write returns false or when audio.$current publishes a different device; further onChanged events in that gesture are ignored until onEnded. The accessibility action re-reads when set returns false. Rejected: showing a read-only bar, which the file comment forbids and which the system's own UI greys out instead. Latching inside SystemVolume as hidden state, because the card owns the gesture.
tasks.acceptance: New tests pass; `swift test --filter AudioWatchTests` stays green; ./scripts/check passes. Live S10: with an HDMI or fixed-volume USB output as default, the lock card shows no volume bar. Dragging the bar while AirPods connect stops the drag, and the AirPods keep their own level.
tasks.risks: G-023 (absolute level on mouse-down, channel balance, mute) and F-045 (device enumeration per pointer event) rewrite the same gesture and SystemVolume.set. Sequence in the media-system lane; this task's set(_:on:) is the seam F-045 wants. KX-10, KX-16 and KX-01 also edit LockScreenCard.swift, in different functions.

tasks.title: The lock-card output picker hears devices plugged in or removed, lists only devices that can be the default, and a failed pick drops the dead row
tasks.why: AudioWatch listens only to DefaultOutputDevice and the default device's volume, never to kAudioHardwarePropertyDevices, so a DAC plugged in while the picker is open never appears. available() filters on output channels and name only, never on DeviceCanBeDefaultDevice or IsHidden. outputRow's `guard AudioOutputs.select(device.id) else { return }` does nothing on a dead id.
files: Tests/IslaKitTests/AudioOutputsTests.swift (new, or the existing symbol test file)
tasks.failing_test_first: (1) A pure `AudioOutputs.offered(_ candidates: [Candidate])` where Candidate carries id, name, outputChannels, canBeDefault, isHidden, transport and dataSource: testHiddenAndNonDefaultDevicesAreNotOffered and testInputOnlyDevicesAreNotOffered. (2) AudioWatchTests.testAFailedPickReReadsTheList: AudioWatch(read:select:) with select returning false and read returning the list without that device; watch.select(id) returns false and outputs no longer contains it. testASuccessfulPickReReadsToo.
tasks.approach: AudioOutputs.available() collects Candidates and filters them through offered(), with two new property reads: kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceCanBeDefaultDevice (output scope) and kAudioDevicePropertyIsHidden. AudioWatch gains an injected `select` closure (default AudioOutputs.select) and a `select(_:) -> Bool` that always refreshes after trying. The glue installs a kAudioHardwarePropertyDevices listener on the system object inside the same install-once guard as the default-output listener, and removes it with that listener; no debounce, because apply() already publishes only what changed. LockScreenCard.outputRow calls audio.select. On true it plays the haptic and returns to the player. On false there is no haptic, the pane stays open, and the re-read has already dropped the dead row. Rejected: a toast or text over the shield, since the lock card has no failure surface and the vanished row is the honest answer. Sharing AmbientWatch's device listener, which has a different lifetime (whole session versus per lock).
tasks.acceptance: Tests pass; ./scripts/check passes. Live S10 (needs hardware): with the picker open while locked, plugging in a USB DAC adds a row within a second, and unplugging a listed device removes it. An aggregate or Loopback sub-device marked as not default-capable is absent.
tasks.risks: F-032 (picker shows only the first five devices), F-053 (selected glyph contrast) and F-026 (watch created per lock) touch outputPicker and the watch's lifetime. Same lane, sequence them. Which virtual devices report CanBeDefault false is hardware-dependent.

tasks.title: A cover over 4 MB arrives downscaled instead of never appearing
tasks.why: The helper base64-encodes ArtworkData as it is. The decoder drops anything over 4 MB, the app asks once, the helper resends the same bytes, and alreadyAsked blocks a third try. Covers embedded at 5-10 MB in local FLAC or ALAC files therefore show the grey note for every track. Above about 9 MB the record also exceeds NDJSONBuffer's 12 MB ceiling.
tasks.failing_test_first: (1) Scripts/test-helper.sh compiles Scripts/helper-tests/artwork_fit_test.m with artwork_fit.m and runs it. The harness draws a 4000x4000 noise PNG with CoreGraphics (over 4 MB), passes it through IslaFitArtwork with a 1.5 MB budget, and asserts that the result is under budget, decodes, and has a longest side of 600 px or less. It also asserts that a 200 KB JPEG comes back byte-identical. It fails today because the function does not exist. (2) NowPlayingPayloadDecoderTests.testArtworkAtTheCapIsKeptAndOverItIsDropped pins the 4 MB contract that the helper now stays under (no decoder test covers the cap today).
tasks.approach: New `NSData *IslaFitArtwork(NSData *data, NSUInteger budget, CGFloat maxSide)`: data at or under budget passes through untouched. Otherwise it makes a CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex thumbnail (CreateThumbnailFromImageAlways, ThumbnailMaxPixelSize 600, WithTransform) and writes it to JPEG at quality 0.85 with CGImageDestination. On any failure it returns nil and the record omits artwork. helper.m calls it just before base64 at the artwork line. bundle.sh compiles both .m files and adds -framework ImageIO -framework CoreGraphics for both architectures. Rejected: raising the Swift cap, because a 13 MB base64 line still crosses the pipe and the NDJSON ceiling every song. Downscaling in Swift, because by then the bytes have already been refused. Re-encoding every cover, which costs CPU per song and changes small covers that are fine.
tasks.acceptance: test-helper.sh passes, including the harness. test-package.sh still finds a two-architecture dylib. ./scripts/check passes. Live: a FLAC with a 6 MB embedded PNG in a Now Playing player shows its cover on the island and the lock card.
tasks.risks: G-008 (uncaught Objective-C exceptions; adds type checks and @try around the same artwork base64 line) must land first or be merged by hand. Run this after it in the media-system lane. F-044 (decode at full resolution) is the Swift-side half and is separate. Memory note: subagents must not dlopen or drive the helper while the owner works; the harness links artwork_fit.m directly and never loads MediaRemote. JPEG drops alpha, which is acceptable for album art.

tasks.title: On the scripting fallback a skip keeps the cover through the same 180 ms grace and same-album rule as the helper route
tasks.why: refreshFromPlayers sets artwork = nil at once on every key change. The helper route waits 180 ms and keeps the cover for an album-mate, a fix filmed on 2026-09-21. DMG users whose helper is Gatekeeper-blocked live on the fallback, and each skip there flashes cover, skeleton, cover.
tasks.failing_test_first: (1) A pure `MediaController.artworkStep(keyChanged:showing:playerChanged:previous:next:) -> ArtworkStep` (.keep, .keepForAlbumMate, .blankAfterGrace): testAnAlbumMateKeepsTheCover and testAnotherAlbumBlanksOnlyAfterTheGrace. (2) MediaControllerTests.testAFallbackSkipWithinTheAlbumNeverShowsTheSkeleton: new seams `playerStateReader` (default PlayerBridge.currentState) and `playerArtworkFetcher` feed two consecutive fallback states on one album; artwork is never nil between them. Fails today, because refreshFromPlayers sets nil.
tasks.approach: Extract the album-mate and grace decision now inlined in the helper branch (:1596-1627) into artworkStep, and call it from both the helper branch and refreshFromPlayers. In the fallback, on a key change: .keepForAlbumMate keeps the image and still fetches, replacing it if the cover differs. .blankAfterGrace schedules the same cancellable blankArtwork Task (180 ms) and fetches, and a fetched image cancels the blank. Rejected: a second copy of the rule in the fallback branch, the same three-copies trap CLAUDE.md records for lyrics. Skipping the fetch for an album-mate, which keeps a wrong cover when an album mixes art.
tasks.acceptance: Tests pass; `swift test --filter MediaControllerTests` and `--filter SkipTransitionTests` stay green; ./scripts/check passes. Live S3 (fallback route): skipping through an album in Music shows one steady cover.
tasks.risks: J-004 (fallback skip keeps the old clock), G-003, G-036 and F-041 (Music artwork script relaunch) all edit refreshFromPlayers or PlayerBridge.artwork. Same lane; the new seams help them too. The lock card's glass flicker in K-011 is closed by KX-16, not here.

tasks.title: Screen-capture pickup remembers only captures taken since it first ran, and over its cap forgets the oldest for good
tasks.why: collect() inserts every capture-shaped name into `seen` before the date test, so a Desktop full of old screenshots fills the 1,000-name cap. trimSeen then keeps `Set(kept.prefix(1000))`, an order that changes with each launch's hash seed, and ShelfStore persists `Array(seen).suffix(1000)`, also arbitrary. Evicted names that postdate `since` come back as cards the user removed.
tasks.failing_test_first: RecordingPickupTests: (1) testAnOldFileIsNeverRemembered: a capture with mtime before since is neither offered nor added to seen, and a second call still does not offer it. This renames and inverts testOldRecordingIsNeverOfferedYetNeverReconsidered, whose seen assertion encodes the bug. (2) testOverTheCapTheOldestAreForgottenAndNeverReturn: 1,005 captures newer than since in a temp folder, all in seen. The result's seen has 1,000 names, its returned since is at least the fifth-oldest mtime, and a second call offers nothing. Today the Set prefix is arbitrary, so recent names can be evicted and re-offered.
tasks.approach: collect(): read the modification date (already prefetched by contentsOfDirectory) before touching seen; at or before `since`, skip without recording, which is free. trimSeen: drop names whose file is gone as today. If still over the cap, sort the survivors by mtime, keep the newest seenLimit, and return the newest evicted mtime as a new floor. fresh() returns `since: max(since, floor)`. ShelfStore persists seen as returned (no suffix) and writes back sinceKey when it rose. Rejected: a larger cap, which delays the failure. An ordered array in defaults, which still needs a date to evict by and grows the stored value.
tasks.acceptance: Both tests pass with the rest of RecordingPickupTests and ShelfStoreTests; ./scripts/check passes.
tasks.risks: G-001 (non-English screenshot prefixes), J-013 (vault ownership by name) and J-021 (folder list) edit RecordingPickup and ShelfStore.importNewRecordings. Same lane. Raising `since` can skip a never-seen file carrying an older mtime (one copied in with preserved dates), which is accepted and stated in the commit body.

tasks.title: A helper that keeps dying after 10 s to a few minutes reaches the fallback instead of being relaunched forever
tasks.why: recordFailure resets its window once 300 s have passed since the first failure, and the delays total 242 s, so a 9th failure inside one window needs lives averaging under about 7 s. A helper that dies every 10-120 s resets to a 2 s delay each window and is relaunched about 2,000 times a day, never falling back and never saying anything.
tasks.failing_test_first: NowPlayingLifecycleTests: testAHelperDyingEveryTenSecondsFallsBack and testAHelperDyingEveryTwoMinutesFallsBack each simulate recordLaunch(now:), then recordFailure 10 s or 120 s later, then a relaunch after the returned delay, and require .fallback within 9 failures. testAHelperThatLivedFiveMinutesIsForgiven: a failure 301 s after launch returns .restart(after: 2). Update the existing case at :58-63 to call recordLaunch, so its 'forgiven after the window' intent is stated as survival time.
tasks.approach: Replace the anchored windowStart with forgiveness by survival: `recordLaunch(now:)` stamps launchedAt. recordFailure forgives (zeroes restartsInWindow) only when now - launchedAt >= window (300 s); an unknown launch counts as zero life. Delays keep escalating from restartsInWindow, and fallback stays at more than 8 restarts or 3 consecutive failures. NowPlayingFeed.launch() calls recordLaunch. Rejected: a sliding 300 s window, because a 30-120 s loop never puts 8 failures inside 300 s. A daily cap, which still relaunches hundreds of times first.
tasks.acceptance: New and updated tests pass; the existing consecutive-failure tests are unchanged and green; ./scripts/check passes.
tasks.risks: G-009 (empty or undecodable records count as healthy) changes recordSuccess and its callers in NowPlayingFeed. Same lane; sequence them. On the fallback, Settings already offers Try Again, so the cost of falling back too early is recoverable.

tasks.title: Spotify scripting stops when Automation is refused, tells an episode or ad from no answer, and accepts a track id only for the song on screen
tasks.why: K-014: updatePrecisionSync never gates on a refusal, so with Spotify Automation denied the 1 Hz loop sends an Apple event and logs an error-level line every second (about 3,600 records an hour, crowding Diagnostics). spotifyTrackID turns 'spotify:episode:…', ads and local files into nil, which requestSpotifyTrackID reads as 'no answer' and retries at 1, 2, 4 and 8 s: five events per episode. K-016: the id script asks for Spotify's current track at execution time, MediaRemote trails Spotify by about a second, and the only guard is the snapshot key, so after a skip the heart can like the new song while the card shows the old one. Both defects live in PlayerBridge.spotifyTrackID and MediaController.requestSpotifyTrackID, so this is one task.
tasks.failing_test_first: (1) Pure `PlayerBridge.spotifyTrackReply(_ raw: String?, title:, artist:)` returning .track(id), .notATrack, .otherSong or .noAnswer: testAnEpisodeIsNotATrack ('spotify:episode:…' gives .notATrack), testTheIdOfTheNextSongIsRefused (uri, name and artist not matching the snapshot gives .otherSong), testAMatchingSongYieldsItsId, and testNothingIsNoAnswer. (2) Pure `MediaController.precisionWanted(isActive:isPlaying:player:lyricsShown:automationDenied:)` is false when automationDenied. (3) Pure `PlayerBridge.recordScriptError(code:app:denied:)` marks Spotify denied on -1743 and not on -1712, and reports whether to log (once per app per session). (4) MediaControllerTests.testAnEpisodeIsAskedOnce: through a new `spotifyTrackIDFetcher` seam returning .notATrack, the fetcher is called exactly once.
tasks.approach: PlayerBridge: the id script returns `id & ASCII character 1 & name & ASCII character 1 & artist` of the current track, the same separator the state script uses. spotifyTrackID completes with spotifyTrackReply against the snapshot's title and artist (trimmed and case-folded). runScript takes an optional PlayerApp; on -1743 it records the app in a lock-guarded session-sticky denied set and logs once at notice level, with later identical codes silent. Other codes log as today. requestSpotifyTrackID: .track sets the id; .notATrack stops; .otherSong and .noAnswer back off as today (the 1 s retry lands after MediaRemote catches up, and the key guard drops the stale track); a denied Spotify is never asked. updatePrecisionSync adds automationDenied through a seam defaulting to PlayerBridge.isDenied. retryNowPlaying(userAsked: true) clears the denied set, so a grant made in System Settings works after Try Again. Add a live-script step: deny Automation, open lyrics for 10 minutes, and count log lines. Rejected: matching the id against the snapshot by duration, which Spotify's script reports in ms and MediaRemote rounds. A permanent denial persisted across launches, which would hide a grant the user makes later.
tasks.acceptance: All new tests pass; `swift test --filter MediaControllerTests` stays green (PlayerBridge.isRunningTests still keeps tests off real Apple events). ./scripts/check passes. Live: with Automation denied, `log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.ctimothe.isla"' --last 10m` shows one -1743 line. A skip followed by a heart tap within a second likes nothing until the card shows the new title.
tasks.risks: J-027 (fallback cannot tell a denied Spotify from 'not playing'), G-005 and J-003 (Automation prompt timing) and F-025 (no AppleScript timeout) all edit runScript or the denial semantics. Whichever lands first owns the denied set, and the others reuse it. Titles with characters G-017 strips (ZWJ, soft hyphen) could compare unequal; compare after the same sanitising, or tolerate .otherSong (it only retries).
tasks.strings_and_tokens: None. Log text is not user-facing.

tasks.title: The lock card keeps one surface across cover changes, so a scrub or volume drag is never torn down mid-gesture
tasks.why: samplesBackdrop = style != .solid && media.artwork == nil switches GlassSurfaceStyle between content.glassEffect and drawn(content) on macOS 26, which changes the identity of everything in the card whenever a cover appears or disappears. That cuts off an in-flight DragGesture without onEnded, leaves scrubbing pinned, and leaves the volume mirror muted. checklist.md already says the lock card's glass is a drawn recipe, because no window above the shield is given a backdrop.
tasks.failing_test_first: LockCardCoverLightTests.testTheCardsSurfaceDoesNotDependOnTheCover: a pure `LockScreenCard.surfaceInputs(style:)` (artwork no longer a parameter) fed into GlassSurfaceStyle(...).usesSystemGlass gives false for every style. A companion check pins that the card's arguments are the same with and without artwork. It fails today, because the no-cover glass case yields system glass on macOS 26. testAScrubStartedOnOneSongNeverSeeksAnother: a pure `LockScreenCard.commitsScrub(startedOn:now:)` is false when the track key changed.
tasks.approach: Pass preferDrawn: true for the lock card and stop deriving samplesBackdrop from artwork, so the modifier always takes the same branch. That matches the checklist's 'drawn recipe' and is the same change F-012 asks for. Latch the track key at the first scrub onChanged, seek in onEnded only if it still matches, and clear scrubbing and draggingVolume in .onChange(of: media.track?.key). Rejected: keeping both modifiers applied and toggling material and opacity, more machinery for a surface that cannot sample anything above the shield anyway. Leaving the identity flip and only resetting drag state, which still kills the gesture.
tasks.acceptance: Tests pass; ./scripts/check passes (visual-lab lock-card renders may need their expectations updated on macOS 26; say so in the commit). Live S10: drag the scrubber across a change from a covered song to a coverless one, and the seek lands or is dropped cleanly, never frozen.

F-003 (contrast over a pale cover) touches coverLight in the same body. The owner judges the lock card's look (memory: apple-design is the bar), so photograph Glass, Transparent and Solid with and without a cover for the visual check.

decisions_made.decision: K-001 and K-002 are one task (KX-01), and so are K-014 and K-016 (KX-15).
decisions_made.reasoning: Each pair rewrites the same functions (refreshSavedState, toggleSaved, refuse and Refusal; PlayerBridge.spotifyTrackID and requestSpotifyTrackID). Two tasks would conflict line by line. K-015 also touches SpotifyAccount but in other functions, so it is a separate task that depends on KX-01.

decisions_made.decision: K-003 is split into the quiet gate plus its Settings row (KX-03) and the Focus filter (KX-04).
decisions_made.reasoning: Each ships on its own. The filter needs a live Focus check and a metadata gate change, and the gate does not.

decisions_made.decision: Quiet means NSApp.currentSystemPresentationOptions containing .fullScreen or .hideMenuBar, or the island's display in a mirror set, or the Focus filter's flag. It is read by pull at gate time.
decisions_made.reasoning: Apple documents the property as the options the active app has in effect system-wide. CGDisplayIsInMirrorSet covers hardware and software mirroring. A pull at the two decision points needs no observers or polling. CGDisplayIsCaptured is deprecated and modern full-screen games set .fullScreen. .autoHideMenuBar alone is ignored to avoid false positives.

decisions_made.decision: The Focus filter parameter defaults to false, and the full-screen switch defaults to on.
decisions_made.reasoning: The system calls perform() with default values when a Focus ends, so the default must mean 'not quiet'. The CEO policy sets the Settings row to default on.

decisions_made.decision: A Spotify refusal re-probes after a 10-minute cooldown and is cleared by Disconnect or a new grant, but not by a token refresh.
decisions_made.reasoning: A refresh is not a new grant, and clearing on refresh would re-enable the API about once an hour. The probe runs from the card header's task, so no dead heart is drawn.

decisions_made.decision: The OAuth scopes stay user-library-read and user-library-modify for the /me/library move.
decisions_made.reasoning: The migration guide says scopes depend on the entity saved. Adding follow and playlist scopes would force every connected user to consent again. A live check confirms the choice.

decisions_made.decision: show_dialog=true is always sent on Connect.
decisions_made.reasoning: Connect is offered only while disconnected, so this matches 'after a disconnect' without persisting a flag.

decisions_made.decision: Helper restarts are forgiven by survival time (alive at least 300 s) instead of a window anchored at the first failure.
decisions_made.reasoning: A sliding 300 s window still never trips for 30-120 s crash loops. Survival-based forgiveness falls back after 8 restarts for any life under 5 minutes.

decisions_made.decision: Oversized covers are downscaled in the helper with ImageIO, only above a 1.5 MB budget, to 600 px JPEG.
decisions_made.reasoning: The bytes are refused before Swift can act, and the pipe and the 12 MB NDJSON ceiling are the real limit. Small covers stay byte-identical.

decisions_made.decision: Screen-capture pickup no longer records names older than `since`, and above the cap it evicts by modification date and raises `since` to the newest evicted date.
decisions_made.reasoning: Raising the floor makes eviction permanent, so a removed card cannot return. The date test reads values contentsOfDirectory already prefetched.

decisions_made.decision: K-017 is closed by giving the lock card the drawn recipe always (preferDrawn: true), the same change F-012 asks for.
decisions_made.reasoning: checklist.md already says the lock card is a drawn recipe above the shield, and this removes the identity flip at its source. Toggling between two modifiers would be more code for a surface that cannot sample anything there.

decisions_made.decision: Spotify, lock-card audio, helper and route tasks sit beside media-system. The Translate and localization tasks and the lock-card surface task sit beside visual-translate. Quiet moments sits beside a11y-shell. Recording pickup sits beside shelf-privacy.
decisions_made.reasoning: Each placement follows the other planners' findings that edit the same functions (G-010, G-032, G-008, G-009, G-023, F-045, J-027 / F-042, G-026, H-007, G-031, F-012 / F-033, G-033, F-013 / G-001, J-021), so each lane can sequence without file conflicts.

deferred.item: Spotify Development Mode limits for the built-in client registration: the app owner must keep an active Premium subscription (the app stops working while it lapses), new apps are capped at 5 users, and applying for extended quota removes both limits.
deferred.reason: Owner-level account decision under CEO policy 4. Trade-off: staying in Development Mode is free and needs no review, but Liked Songs then works only for listed accounts and dies whenever the owner's Premium lapses. Extended quota needs Spotify's review and an app that meets their criteria. Closes the open checklist.md:654 item. KX-01's copy is written to stay true either way.

deferred.item: Expanding OAuth scopes if /me/library refuses track URIs with only the user-library scopes (the reference pages also list user-follow-* and playlist-* scopes).
deferred.reason: Changing an account's scopes forces every connected user to consent again and counts as touching an account (CEO policy 1). Decide only if the KX-01 live check shows Spotify demands them, then record it in checklist.md.

deferred.item: Developer ID signing so the media helper is not Gatekeeper-blocked, which would take most DMG users off the scripting fallback that K-011 (KX-12) and K-014 (KX-15) polish.
deferred.reason: Owner-level decision (CEO policy 4; memory: isla-gatekeeper-dylib-block). Trade-off: a paid Apple Developer membership and a notarization pipeline, against every ad-hoc DMG user seeing a malware alert and losing the helper route. KX-12 and KX-15 are worth doing either way.

deferred.item: Detecting short Ukrainian words that carry none of ї, є or ґ (for example 'Дякую').
deferred.reason: No letter rule can separate them from Russian. They depend on Apple's recognizer confidence, which round 3 left as live-only. KX-07 fixes every word that has a distinguishing letter.

deferred.item: Whether peeks and the hot-key panel sit above Keynote and PowerPoint play windows and display-captured games, and whether those apps set .hideMenuBar while playing.
deferred.reason: Live-only (round-3 'what remains'). KX-03 adds the S12 step. If a slideshow sets neither .fullScreen nor .hideMenuBar, add a check for a frontmost screen-sized window then, not speculatively.
